lines.text: This is FlipTheMeme. Every minute a new round opens on a busy memecoin whose PumpSwap pool is only minutes old. And crypto Twitter is already arguing about it, live, right on top.
The price is the token's price in SOL, read every second from its PumpSwap pool on mainnet. You call UP or DOWN without buying the token. A one-minute move, result in about two minutes.

I tap UP. Mobile Wallet Adapter opens the Seeker's own Seed Vault Wallet once. One approval deposits test SOL into my in-app vault, opens a limited device session. The default is one hour and 0.02 SOL per call. My original call goes in only if that round is still open and the exact amount still fits. That key can only place bets; the program gives it no way to withdraw.
From now on every call is one tap, with no wallet pop-up. My pixel face joins the UP side, and it travels inside the bet itself.

Rounds are matched one to one. Only the amount both sides cover plays, and any surplus comes back without a fee. On devnet a house account can fill the short side, capped on chain per round and per day, so a solo player can still get a matched round.

The start price is not the price when I tapped. It is the average of ten seconds that start thirty seconds after entry closes, so it is still unknown when anyone taps. Then comes the one-minute move. Green above the line, red below.

A win pays 1.96 times the matched part of the stake. The attestor samples the pool and publishes one signed certificate for the window. The keeper relays that same certificate. Both services are currently run by our team. The program does the math on chain and credits my vault, the signed samples stay in the transaction. I see my matched stake, refund and net result, then the next round’s token before repeating.

Then I challenge a friend. The card goes out with a link: the page asks them to take the other side, and with the app installed one tap opens the round. And if I leave the app, a notification brings me back when the round is over.
FlipTheMeme. Built for Seeker, live on Solana devnet today. Pick a side.
